Baram v0.7.5 gives you ways to type the characters that are not on your keyboard, turns
much more of how the app looks into settings you can adjust, and adds a Focus perspective
that clears most of the bars and panels away from the document.

If you are updating from v0.7.4, these are the changes most likely to catch you out:
**choosing the Writing perspective now closes the sidebar**, as its description always
said it would; **numbered lists line their numbers up on the first digit**, where they
used to line up on the period; **perspectives have moved to Settings › Layout**; and if you
use Tokyo Night, Nord, Solarized or Baram Garden, **callouts, git markers and parts of the
graph now take the theme's colours**. Renaming a note also updates the block references
and embeds that point at it now, not only its `[[links]]`.

---

# New and improved

## Symbols, emoji and smart punctuation

Until now Baram had no way of its own to put `→` or `≤` in a note except an inline
formula, which saves formula syntax to the file instead of the character. There are three
ways now, and all three write the character itself — a `:smile` you pick becomes `😄` in
the markdown, not a `:smile:` shortcode — so the file reads the same in any editor.

- **Type `:` and two letters of a name.** A menu of matching symbols and emoji opens at the
  caret: `:arrow` offers `→`, `:heart` offers `❤️`, `:+1` offers `👍️`. It searches 79
  symbols and 1,845 emoji by English and Korean keywords (`:화살표`, `:웃음`), and a
  complete GitHub shortcode such as `:smile` puts that emoji first. The `:` has to start a
  word, so `10:30`, `https://` and `key: value` never open it, and it stays closed in code
  and while you edit a formula. It is on by default; **Settings › Markdown › Typography ›
  Symbol & Emoji Suggestions** turns it off.
- **A picker for the ones you cannot name.** Type `/` and choose **Symbols & Emoji** to browse
  a grid with a search box, tabs for recent picks, for symbols and for each emoji group, and
  the name of the highlighted character. **Recently used** keeps the last 24 characters you
  inserted, from the picker or from the `:` menu, and survives a restart.
- **Smart punctuation does something now.** The switch has sat in Settings › Markdown since
  February, and nothing in the editor ever read it. Turned on, it replaces `->` `<-` `<->`
  `=>` `<=` `>=` `!=` `<=>` `--` `...` with `→ ← ↔ ⇒ ≤ ≥ ≠ ⇔ — …` as you type, and
  **Backspace** straight afterwards takes the replacement back (`<->` and `<=>` step back
  one stage at a time). Code, maths, a link or wikilink you have not closed yet, a tag, an
  HTML comment, pasted text and skill files are left as written. It stays **off by
  default**.

## Adjust how the app looks, one dial at a time

v0.7.4 had two appearance dials. There are fourteen now. A dial you change is marked
**Custom** and gets its own revert, so you can put one back without touching the rest; a
dial your theme sets is marked **Theme**; a dial with no mark is on Baram's default and
writes nothing, so the stylesheet decides.

**Settings › Appearance**

- **Accent hue** and **Accent saturation** turn the current theme's accent colour around the
  colour wheel, or make it more or less vivid. They move the theme's own accent rather than
  replacing it, so they carry over when you change themes.
- **Light background contrast** and **Dark background contrast** decide how far the
  sidebars, activity bar, tab bar and status bar stand apart from the document: *Flat* gives
  them the document's colour, and *All white* (light) or *True black* (dark) paints the
  document and the bars alike. There is one per mode, so a theme that follows your system
  picks up the right one when the system switches.
- **Density** (Compact / Default / Spacious) and **Corners** (Sharp / Default / Round) scale
  the spacing and rounding across the interface. Pill and circle shapes keep their shape,
  and the document keeps its own paragraph spacing and padding, which are editor settings.

To give those two dials something to move, the interface's spacing and corners were put on
one shared scale. Most values were on it already; about three hundred that were not moved to
the nearest step, nearly all of them one to four pixels smaller, so some panels sit a
little tighter than before even at the default setting. Code in the AI chat now uses the
app's own code font.

**Settings › Editor**, under Display — how the document itself is set, with Korean text in
mind:

- **Line breaking** — *Keep words whole (Korean)* stops a line from breaking in the middle
  of a Korean word. A long URL still wraps.
- **Letter spacing** (−0.05 to +0.1em) and **Paragraph spacing** (0 to 2em).
- **Emphasis style** — draw `*emphasis*` in italic, in the accent colour, or bolder. Korean
  typefaces seldom have a real italic, so the slanted text is usually a distorted copy of the
  upright one.
- **List guide strength** — the faint vertical line in nested lists can be made fainter,
  stronger, or hidden at 0.
- **List number alignment** — *Align numbers* keeps every number the same distance from its
  fold arrow as the digits pile up, and is the new default. *Align periods* is the old look,
  with the periods in one column. The fold arrows also sit a little further from the markers
  in both kinds of list, and a short list that starts at `2.` no longer reserves room for a
  digit it never uses.

## Themes reach more of the screen

A theme set about two dozen colours — text, backgrounds, borders, the accent, three status
colours and the basic graph colours — and most of the rest stayed on Baram's default
palette whatever you picked: callouts, git markers, the rest of the graph (orphan, pinned,
tag and neighbour nodes, labels), some status colours, and the hover and selection
backgrounds. Tokyo Night's callouts were the same emerald and violet as everyone else's.
Those colours are now worked out from the theme's own — for Tokyo Night, Nord, the two
Solarized and the two Baram Garden themes, and for any theme you make. Default Light and
Default Dark are Baram's default palette, so they look as they did. The Theme Editor has one
new colour, **List Guide**, for the tint of that vertical line in nested lists.

For theme authors: a theme package can now suggest values for the dials above and whether
the three bars start hidden, and the installer warns — without refusing — when a palette
misses WCAG AA contrast. No themes are published yet, so nothing uses either today.

## Focus, and bars you can hide

- **Focus** is a fifth built-in perspective (`Cmd+Alt+5` / `Ctrl+Alt+5`). It hides the
  sidebar, the right panel, the activity bar, the status bar and the tab bar. The strip of
  open folders and vaults along the top stays.
- **The activity bar, status bar and tab bar can each be hidden on their own** — `Cmd+Alt+A`,
  `Cmd+Alt+S` and `Cmd+Alt+B` (`Ctrl+Alt+…` on Windows and Linux), or **Settings › Layout ›
  Show or Hide**. Hiding a bar only stops it being drawn: hiding the tab bar does not close
  your tabs. With all three hidden, point at or Tab to the top edge of the window for a
  **Reveal hidden bars** button.
- Bars you hide come back when Baram restarts. To keep a layout, save it as a perspective.
- **Choosing a perspective now applies its layout exactly.** The Writing perspective is
  described as "Hide sidebar and focus on the editor", but a perspective could only ever open
  the sidebar, never close it, so Writing left the sidebar alone and closed only the right
  panel. It closes the sidebar now,
  and so does Focus. Your expanded folders stay expanded, and `Cmd+Shift+L` /
  `Ctrl+Shift+L` brings the sidebar back. Closing a Journal or Zettel context tab still
  returns you to Writing without closing a sidebar you had open.
- The Activity Bar settings tab is now called **Layout**, and perspectives moved there from
  Appearance.

---

# Fixed

## Renaming a note updates block references and embeds

Renaming a note rewrote `[[note]]` and left `((note#^id))` and `{{embed ((note#^id))}}`
pointing at the old name, so they broke with nothing said. All three are rewritten now,
including the references a note makes to itself. So are two kinds of `[[link]]` that were
missed before: one written with its extension, `[[note.md]]`, which keeps the `.md`, and one
that capitalises an accented or non-Latin name (É, Ω, Д) differently from the file. A block
reference written with a folder path, `((folder/note#^id))`, is still not updated.

When the new name cannot be written as a link — `C# notes`, where the `#` would start a
heading anchor, or a name that ends in `.md` or a space — the links are left alone and a
notice tells you how many files may still point at the old name. Before, `[[note]]` quietly
became `[[C# notes]]`, which is a link to a note called `C`. If the note you renamed links
to itself and has unsaved edits, the notice now says that saving them will write the old
name back.

## Keyboard

- **Option+← and Option+→ move by word on macOS.** They were being taken as Back and Forward
  through your tab history whenever there was any. Windows and Linux keep Alt+← / Alt+→ as
  Back and Forward.
- **Ctrl+- did two things at once** — it zoomed out and went Back, on every platform. Zoom
  now uses `Cmd` on macOS and `Ctrl` elsewhere, and `Ctrl+-` / `Ctrl+Shift+-` as Back and
  Forward are macOS only.

## Editing

- **Inserting a horizontal rule no longer throws the caret to the end of the document** when
  there is something below it. `---`, the slash menu, the command palette and the menu
  command all had this.

## Windows

- **Renaming a folder now updates relative links that spell it in a different case.**
  `[[./NS/c]]` and `[[./ns/c]]` are the same place on Windows, but only the drive letter was
  compared without case, so such links were neither updated nor reported. Network (UNC) paths
  had the same problem. Only the letters A to Z are compared without case.

## Plugins

- **Release builds no longer load development plugin folders from the settings file.** The
  list of those folders is kept in `config.json`, which the app's own web view can write, and
  release builds refused to *add* a folder but still *loaded* every one already on the list —
  on each launch, with no consent record, and exempt from the withdrawal list. If you
  sideloaded a folder under v0.4.x, or added one from a development build on this machine,
  the release app now ignores it. Development builds are unchanged.

## Settings

- **Editor padding can be found by searching settings.** It was never registered with the
  search.
- **The settings window's icons come from one icon set and line up in the tab list.** A mix
  of icons and text symbols sat a few pixels apart from each other.

---

**Updating.** Press **Install & Restart** in the update dialog and Baram installs in place
and restarts. Linux `.deb` and `.rpm` cannot be updated in place by the updater; those, and
any install that fails, open the releases page instead.
